limitations: Checks lazy frame creation, tab state and draft guards; real iframe rendering is separately checked in Chrome.

results.description: Restoring four tabs creates only the active iframe, keeping every tab and its order.
The active restored iframe has the correct route and retains the QA namespace.
Saved active tab, expanded menu, sidebar position and collapsed state survive restore.
Declining a dirty editor leave keeps the current tab and does not create the destination iframe.
Accepting a dirty editor leave loads a restored inactive tab on its first sidebar visit.
Returning to a visited tab reuses its existing iframe and in-memory state.
Closing an unvisited restored tab removes only tab state without creating an iframe.
Declining close of a dirty active tab retains its iframe and the unvisited neighbor.
Closing the active tab activates and creates its previously unvisited adjacent tab.
Close-others retains a loaded background tab when its dirty-editor guard declines.
Close-others removes accepted background frames while retaining the active frame.
Closing the last tab clears the active route and frames without creating replacements.
A sidebar route remains usable after all restored tabs have been closed.
Only the isolated shell navigation key changes; unrelated stored business data is preserved.
An explicit URL route wins over the saved active tab and still creates one iframe.
Legacy session-tab restore also loads only the active iframe.
Duplicate and unavailable restored tabs are filtered before lazy activation.
The synthetic harness performs only its stubbed navigation fetch and has no DOM runtime errors.
